title: How do we write halves, quarters and fifths as decimals?
description: Six fractions made from halves, quarters and fifths are written as decimals by making the bottom number ten or a hundred. A last step multiplies one answer back.
teaching_notes: One idea: multiply the top and bottom by the same number to make the bottom ten or a hundred. Watch for children who multiply only the bottom number.

source: Figure it Out (end of chapter), Q16
video_script.why: The child has written fractions with bottom numbers ten, a hundred and a thousand as decimals and now meets bottom numbers two, four and five.
video_script.substitution: Multiply the top and bottom by the same number to make the bottom ten or a hundred, then read off the decimal.
video_script.anchor: six fractions made from halves, quarters and fifths
video_script.payoff_line: Make the bottom number ten or a hundred, then read off the decimal

final_answer.spoken: zero point five, one point five, zero point two five, zero point seven five, zero point two and zero point eight

video_script.fraction_reading: halves, quarters and fifths are said as words
maths_rules: check: 4 x 0.25 = 1, and four quarters make one whole
video_script.design: The six fractions stay in the anchor band; each family of fractions is multiplied top and bottom to ten or a hundred in the working band, and a last step multiplies 0.25 by four.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; six fractions (a) 1/2 (b) 3/2 (c) 1/4 (d) 3/4 (e) 1/5 (f) 4/5; a question mark in the anchor band
narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about changing common fractions into decimals.
<bookmark mark='list'/>Six fractions are given, made from halves, quarters and fifths.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Write each fraction in decimal form.

beats.on_screen: the fractions stay on the board; Keeko sits beside them as the child
narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a place value chart with tenths and hundredths; a fraction bar whose top and bottom are both multiplied by the same number

marks.easy: tenths and hundredths are marked on the chart
marks.same: top and bottom are multiplied by the same number and the fraction keeps its size

narration: <bookmark mark='easy'/>A fraction is quick to write as a decimal when the bottom number is ten or a hundred.
<bookmark mark='same'/>We can reach ten or a hundred by multiplying the top and bottom by the same number.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, one half and three halves, one quarter and three quarters, and one fifth and four fifths.

beats.on_screen: To find: each fraction in decimal form
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each fraction in decimal form.

marks.half: top and bottom of 1/2 are multiplied by 5

narration: <bookmark mark='half'/>Step one, multiply the top and bottom of a half by five, which makes five over ten.
<bookmark mark='halfw'/>That is zero point five.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Three halves becomes fifteen over ten, which is one point five.

marks.q: top and bottom of 1/4 are multiplied by 25

narration: <bookmark mark='q'/>Step two, multiply the top and bottom of a quarter by twenty-five.
<bookmark mark='qw'/>That makes twenty-five over a hundred, which is zero point two five.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Three quarters becomes seventy-five over a hundred, which is zero point seven five.

marks.f: top and bottom of 1/5 are multiplied by 2

narration: <bookmark mark='f'/>Step three, multiply the top and bottom of a fifth by two.
<bookmark mark='fw'/>That makes two over ten, which is zero point two.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Four fifths becomes eight over ten, which is zero point eight.
<bookmark mark='chk'/>Step four, put one answer back by taking four of zero point two five.
<bookmark mark='same'/>Four times zero point two five is one, and four quarters make one whole too.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Make the bottom number ten or a hundred, then read off the decimal.
<bookmark mark='h'/>The halves are zero point five and one point five.
<bookmark mark='q'/>The quarters are zero point two five and zero point seven five.
<bookmark mark='f'/>The fifths are zero point two and zero point eight.
